subject: geography
title: Hazard Classification & Vulnerability
welcome_lead: Classify hazards and explore risk equations.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on hazard classification, vulnerability and risk perception.
final_note: Risk depends on hazard, exposure and vulnerability.

concepts.def: Natural event with potential to cause harm to people and property.
Probability of harm; Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability x Exposure / Capacity.
Susceptibility to harm; influenced by income, governance, infrastructure.
Capacity to absorb shock and recover quickly.
Size or strength of event (e.g. Richter, VEI, Saffir-Simpson).
How often event occurs; inverse relationship with magnitude usually.

walkthroughs.body_html: Tectonic hazards include earthquakes, volcanoes, tsunamis. Atmospheric hazards include tropical cyclones, droughts, heatwaves. Hydrological include floods, landslides. Biological include pandemics. Multi-hazard events (e.g. Tohoku 2011) compound risk.
Haiti 2010 (Mw 7.0) killed 220000; Chile 2010 (Mw 8.8, 500x more energy) killed 525. Difference lies in vulnerability: GDP per capita, building codes, governance. Risk is not just hazard magnitude.

Fatalism (it is God's will), domination (we can control nature) and adaptation (mitigate and prepare) shape responses. Wealthy nations invest in early warning (e.g. Japan tsunami sirens); poorer nations rely on community responses.
